reason: NFAJ's non-film collection portal 'Japanese Film Heritage' (https://nfajfilmheritage.jp/, a Nuxt SPA) is backed by a first-party Elasticsearch API on the museum's own host: POST https://jfh.nfaj.go.jp/v2/elasticsearch/search (HTTP Basic auth jfhapi:backend202403, the key shipped in the public _nuxt/constants.*.js bundle). Index archive_v5_2 holds 6,999 docs across 4 material genres (資料ジャンル): ポスター(posters) 219, 映画館チラシ(cinema flyers/chirashi) 873, 映画館プログラム(cinema programmes) 5,682, 技術資料(camera/projector equipment) 225. We collect the three FLAT print genres and EXCLUDE 技術資料 (3D equipment, out of scope). Of the flat-art docs, 5,532 carry downloadable high-res cover images; after the min-4 guard (year required; only 2 records lack an artist) the FINAL collectable set is 4,754 records (programmes 4,422 + posters 153 + flyers 179). Images are served at https://jfh.nfaj.go.jp/images/{path} in 360px/1200px/3200px tiers — verified well above 600px: poster 3200px = 2363×3200, 1200px = 886×1200; flyer 1200px = 927×1200; and the autocropped R2 webp = 1512×2048. Rich Japanese metadata per record (title, English title, director/publisher, year, dimensions, cinema, films shown, collection). This is the museum's own flat film-poster art, NOT moving-image title records.
easy_source_found: No formal open-data/portal (nfaj.go.jp/opendata, /api, /sitemap.xml, /robots.txt all 404). BUT a de-facto machine-readable first-party API exists: the 'Japanese Film Heritage' non-film portal (nfajfilmheritage.jp, Nuxt SSG) fetches from https://jfh.nfaj.go.jp/v2/elasticsearch/search at runtime with Basic auth (jfhapi:backend202403) embedded in the public JS bundle. Returns full Elasticsearch _source JSON. (NFAJ also exposes OPAC opac.nfaj.go.jp, a film-collection DB nfad.nfaj.go.jp, and a Japan Search dataset jpsearch.go.jp/database/nfad, but those are moving-image/library catalogues, not flat-art image sources.)
probe_summary: node scripts/scrape-nfaj.mjs --probe collected 15/15 works (5 posters + 5 flyers + 5 programmes), 0 image errors, 0 min-4 drops. R2 upload verified publicly retrievable: HTTP 200 image/webp 1512×2048 (autocropped from a 3200px source). All 8 standard fields 100% filled on the probe set. Output: /Users/kietzsche/armin-web-main/public/data/nfaj-collection-probe.json. The ES endpoint chokes on any `query` object (1-byte body) but honours {from,size} pagination + {size:0,aggs} — so the scraper pages the whole index and filters genre client-side on _source.data.資料ジャンル.content. jfh.nfaj.go.jp serves an incomplete TLS chain, so the script sets NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 (first-party host; curl/macOS keychain accepts it). DID NOT run --full.

exhibitions_entry.name: National Film Archive of Japan
exhibitions_entry.description: The National Film Archive of Japan (NFAJ) in Kyobashi, Tokyo is the country's only national institution dedicated to film, and the seventh of Japan's national art museums. Independent since 2018 (formerly the National Film Center of the National Museum of Modern Art), it preserves more than 80,000 film titles alongside an exhaustively gathered non-film collection of posters, cinema flyers (chirashi), theatre programmes, stills and apparatus. Its 'Japanese Film Heritage' digital portal opens this paper heritage to the public — vintage Japanese film posters from the 1910s onward, illustrated cinema handbills, and richly designed theatre programmes documenting a century of moviegoing culture.
exhibitions_entry.description_ko: 도쿄 교바시에 자리한 국립영화아카이브(NFAJ)는 일본에서 영화만을 전문으로 다루는 유일한 국립기관이자, 일곱 번째 국립미술관이다. 본래 도쿄국립근대미술관의 필름센터였다가 2018년 독립했으며, 8만여 편의 영화 필름과 더불어 포스터, 영화관 전단(치라시), 극장 프로그램, 스틸, 영사·촬영 기재를 망라해 수집해 왔다. '일본영화유산(Japanese Film Heritage)' 디지털 포털은 이 지면 유산을 일반에 공개한다. 1910년대부터 이어진 일본 영화 포스터, 삽화가 담긴 영화관 전단, 정교하게 디자인된 극장 프로그램이 한 세기에 걸친 영화 관람 문화를 보여준다.

notes: Source = jfh.nfaj.go.jp Elasticsearch (index archive_v5_2). API quirks the scraper handles: (1) the endpoint returns a 1-byte body for any request containing a `query` key, so it ONLY supports {from,size} paging (total via hits.total.value=6999) plus {size:0,aggs:{terms:{field:'search.genre.keyword'}}} — genre filtering is therefore client-side on _source.data.資料ジャンル.content; (2) the jfh subdomain ships an incomplete TLS cert chain (node fetch → UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE) so NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 is set in-script. Category mapping: posters/flyers/programmes → 'print' (all are flat film-poster/graphic art; per the film-museum scope + GUIDE §1 they are NEVER colour-gated, so colorfulness() is copied but not used to drop). 'artist' = publisher (発行者) or director (監督); records with no parseable 4-digit year (~776, mostly chirashi dated ????.MM.DD) and the 2 with no creator are dropped by the min-4 guard per GUIDE §2 (no Unknown placeholders). Multi-page docs: one ARMIN record = the COVER image (first of data.images, 3200px→1200px→360px). Projected full JSON ≈ 3.8 MB (well under 24 MB), so no cap/prioritization is required, though the scraper orders posters→flyers→programmes for curatorial quality. Full ETA ~45 min at CONC=5 (4,754 image downloads + autocrop + R2). Coords = 3-7-6 Kyobashi, Chuo-ku, Tokyo 104-0031 (Google Maps place pin). Run `node scripts/scrape-nfaj.mjs --full` (resumable via scripts/.state/nfaj-progress.json; failures → nfaj-failed.ndjson) then Phase F (prefix-collection-ids already applied in-script via nfaj- prefix; register in exhibitions.js + restart Vite).
